request: why is the median sometimes better than the mean?

beats.intent: Five house prices as dots on a number line: 3, 4, 5, 6 and 50 (hundred thousand)
beats.narration: Five houses on a street sell for three, four, five and six hundred thousand, and one mansion for five million.
beats.code:
stage.title("Mean or median?")
nl = draw_number_line(stage, x_range=(0, 50))
for v in (3, 4, 5, 6, 50):
    mark_point(stage, nl, v, color=YELLOW)
stage.caption("prices in £100 000s")

beats.intent: The mean 13.6 marked, far from every ordinary house
beats.narration: The mean adds them and divides by five: thirteen point six. That's more than twice any ordinary house.
beats.code: mean = mark_point(stage, nl, 13.6, color=RED, label="mean 13.6", direction=UR)

beats.intent: The median 5 marked in the middle of the four close dots
beats.narration: The median is the middle price when they're in order: five. It ignores how extreme the mansion is, so it describes a typical house better.
beats.code:
med = mark_point(stage, nl, 5, color=GREEN, label="median 5", direction=UL)
stage.caption("mean = 68 ÷ 5 = 13.6, median = 5")

request: if you double the sides of a square, what happens to its area?

beats.intent: A 1 by 1 square next to a 2 by 2 square split into four unit squares
beats.narration: Take a square with side one. Double the side to two.
beats.code:
stage.title("Double the side")
small = Square(1.0, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to([-4, -0.8, 0])
big = VGroup(*[Square(1.0, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(4)]).arrange_in_grid(rows=2, cols=2, buff=0).move_to([-1, -0.3, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(small), FadeIn(big))
stage.add(small, big)
stage.label(small, "1", direction=DOWN, color=BLUE)
stage.label(big, "2", direction=DOWN, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: A 3 by 3 square of nine unit squares beside them
beats.narration: The doubled square holds four of the small ones, not two. Triple the side and it holds nine.
beats.code:
bigger = VGroup(*[Square(1.0, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(9)]).arrange_in_grid(rows=3, cols=3, buff=0).move_to([3.2, 0.2, 0])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(s) for s in bigger], lag_ratio=0.1))
stage.add(bigger)
stage.label(bigger, "3", direction=DOWN, color=ORANGE)
stage.caption("areas 1, 4, 9")

beats.intent: The squares beside area × k² when sides × k
beats.narration: Scale the sides by k and the area scales by k squared. That's true of any shape, not just squares.

request: how many ways can 4 people sit in a row?

beats.intent: Four empty seats and four people A, B, C, D
beats.narration: Four people, four seats in a row.
beats.code:
stage.title("Arranging 4 people")
seats = VGroup(*[Square(1.1, color=GREY_B) for _ in range(4)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3).move_to([0, 0.8, 0])
stage.play(Create(seats))
stage.add(seats)
people = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color=c, fill_opacity=0.8) for c in (BLUE, GREEN, ORANGE, RED)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5).move_to([0, -1.2, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(people))
stage.add(people)
for p, n in zip(people, "ABCD"):
    stage.label(p, n, direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: The number of choices written under each seat: 4, 3, 2, 1
beats.narration: The first seat can take any of four people. Then three are left for the second, two for the third, one for the last.
beats.code:
for s, n in zip(seats, "4321"):
    t = Text(n, font_size=40, color=YELLOW).move_to(s)
    stage.play(FadeIn(t), run_time=0.3)
    stage.add(t)

beats.narration: Multiply the choices: twenty four different orders. That product is called four factorial.

request: how does an arch bridge hold up heavy loads?

beats.intent: A stone arch spanning a river between two banks
beats.narration: An arch bridge curves over the river, resting on the banks at each end.
beats.code:
stage.title("An arch bridge")
river = Rectangle(width=8, height=0.6, stroke_width=0, fill_color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to([0, -2.4, 0])
bank_l = Rectangle(width=2, height=1.2, color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=0.6).move_to([-5, -2.1, 0])
bank_r = Rectangle(width=2, height=1.2, color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=0.6).move_to([5, -2.1, 0])
arch = ArcBetweenPoints([-4, -1.5, 0], [4, -1.5, 0], angle=-PI * 0.7, color=ORANGE, stroke_width=14)
deck = Line([-6, 0.9, 0], [6, 0.9, 0], color=GREY_B, stroke_width=8)
stage.play(FadeIn(river), FadeIn(bank_l), FadeIn(bank_r), Create(arch), Create(deck))
stage.add(river, bank_l, bank_r, arch, deck)

beats.intent: A heavy load pressing down in the middle and arrows following the curve of the arch down to both banks
beats.narration: A lorry presses down in the middle. The arch turns that downward push into squeezing along its curve, out to both ends.
beats.code:
load = Square(0.8, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to([0, 1.4, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(load, shift=DOWN))
stage.add(load)
down = Arrow([0, 1.0, 0], [0, 0.0, 0], buff=0, color=RED)
stage.play(GrowArrow(down))
stage.add(down)
for t0, t1 in ((0.5, 0.15), (0.5, 0.85)):
    a = Arrow(arch.point_from_proportion(t0), arch.point_from_proportion(t1), buff=0, color=YELLOW, path_arc=-0.6 if t1 < t0 else 0.6)
    stage.play(GrowArrow(a))
    stage.add(a)
stage.caption("the load becomes squeeze along the arch")

beats.intent: The banks pushing back inward and upward at the feet of the arch
beats.narration: At the ends, the banks push back, inward and up. Stone is very strong when squeezed, so arches have stood for two thousand years.
beats.code:
for x, d in ((-4, np.array([0.8, 1.0, 0])), (4, np.array([-0.8, 1.0, 0]))):
    a = Arrow([x, -1.5, 0] - d, [x, -1.5, 0], buff=0, color=GREEN)
    stage.play(GrowArrow(a))
    stage.add(a)
stage.caption("the banks push back: stone loves squeezing")
